item.title: Spartacus (2010)
item.description:
It's a story related to a big slave rebellion in Roman republic before Rome became an empire. There was a Thracian soldier (modern day Bulgaria), Spartacus, who served in Roman army for a long time, around ten years, but due to some disagreement with the army general he was punished and pushed into slavery. Later he rose to become a popular gladiator and led fellow slaves to rebel, which lasted for many years and shook Roman republic. His defeat gave a way to the first dictator of Roman empire, Gaius Julius Ceaser.

Now on top of this story, add some sex, nudity, and violence, which is a popular way in modern movie makers to tell Roman history. It does not need to be like this because they can show stoicism, philosophy, and some goodness in people, but it is like this.

I want to point out one special thing in this series. The lead actor, Andy Whitfield, who played Spartacus did it really well but he left after first series because he got cancer. Sadly, he never recovered completely and died. After Andy a new lead actor, Liam McIntyre, took the role of Spartacus but the series could not gain same interest. Liam did a good job in acting but I am not sure what went wrong.

Overall, it's a nice TV series especially for history lover, who can tolerate blood and violence. So I recommend it with 3 stars.

item.title: Tenzing (2026)
item.description:
I love watching mountain movies as a part of armchair travel fantasies because I don't have enough strength, time, or money to even try climbing above eight thousand meter peaks. This movie fits in both categories—mountains and traveling. It's a story of the famous expedition of Mt. Everest where Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay summited the peak successfully for the first time in human history. However, contrary to ignoring Sherpas which most of the movies did in past, this time the storytelling is done from the perception of Tenzing.

This movie brings the story of Tenzing who was born in Tibet but later migrated to Nepal with his parents who left him in a village when he got sick during the migratory journey. He grew up as a servant boy, and during his childhood his first encounter with mountaineering was with George Mallory who later inspired him to break the shackles of mundane life and climb the unthinkable Goddess, Chomolungma, aka Mr. Everest. And whole world knows that he did succeed in it.

I think mesmerizing scenery complemented with beautiful music is the perfect recipe for a mountain movie. This movie combines it with human journey, making it a unique experience for the audience. I highly recommend it with 4 stars.

item.title: We Dont Need No Innovation
item.description:
Nowadays, new tech gadgets are being released at an increasingly faster pace than ever before. Every week there is either a new cutting-edge foldable-pro-max-biggest-screen-ever smartphone or a jumping, flying box-like car with revolutionary rocket tech. And do not forget that new AI model which will make your charlatan boss look smarter, and help him cut the budget by firing half of the team. I know I have made many assumptions here, but bear with me.

Despite these amazing advancements in engineering, I feel less excited and more skeptical with each passing year. I do not understand their purpose or how safe they are, as not much research has been done about their impact. Also, there is a big problem of privacy, where our activities are being tracked.

Perhaps it's my age, as I am getting older (still early thirties, though), or perhaps we as a society fucked up again. I still prefer to take the blame on my age, but why do I then check the launch of new gadgets on YouTube? I think I still look forward to that excitement. And if this is all about age, then why, in these launches, are most of the people older than me (I rarely see a guy in his twenties there)? One example is the new iPhone duo—Jeez, I feel stupefied just thinking about it. I do not understand what is the rush for buying 2-3k $ phone. Maybe your billionaire pocket is so heavy that you can not control it, or you are just an influencer (YouTuber) who wants to snatch it first to get more views. If it's the latter case, dude, you are riding the wave of capitalism just to mess with the minds of young ones. Anyway, none of that impresses me. My refurbished iPhone 13 mini is more than enough to do almost anything. And if I want to appreciate the new technical marvel, I will go to Apple's store, check it out, and then leave.

Fifteen years ago, when I was in my early twenties, I got my first laptop, a Sony Vaio E-series. Then the following year, I got my first LG touchscreen smartphone. Those were a big deal for me, as no one in my family ever used a laptop or a touchscreen phone. At that time, people used to be so surprised/jealous/in-awe seeing a new gadget in someone else's hand that they would come and ask about it. Once, on a train, a girl approached me to check out my new fancy phone. Just thinking about that time makes me excited. The same thing was with cars and motorbikes. My friends and I used to watch automobile shows on Discovery Channel and discuss the specs of new Ferraris or Bugattis, such as engine, acceleration, torque, and top speed. But then something changed that led to the current situation.

I wonder many times about what exactly went wrong. It might be that we passed the peak of development needed to build a prosperous society, and now these new gadgets are just tricks to keep the buzz going. It's similar to a drug addict: we want new shots to feel the same as we felt the first time, but now it's just hurting our health. That is why we see useless and expensive gadgets, pushing the boundaries of biology and psychology just to create a new buzz. AI gadgets, Neuralink chips, AR/XR glasses, and Virtual Reality gadgets are a few more examples here. The worst part is that these techs are advancing so fast that we, as a society, have a hard time studying their impact and building laws for their use cases. The companies behind these fancy tech often claim, with their biased research, that they want to help people with some kind of disability. However, after experiencing the mess they created with social media, it is hard for me to put my trust in them again.

Now in my thirties, I feel my nostalgic moments are guiding me—at least I have those memories, unlike new generations. They remind me that I do not need all those new superhuman gadgets to be happy. I should hold on to whatever I have for now, and reduce my gadget dependence. That does not mean I want to be a tech-hermit, as I love self-hosting and playing with local AI models. I just don't want to spend money for momentarily pleasures in buying stuff, but on my hobbies and health, to gain some satisfaction and peace in life.

What about you? Do you also feel the same?

item.title: Moonlight Mile
item.description:
A young man, Joe, whose fiance died in a homicide just few days before the wedding tries to cope up with grief and emotionally supports his parents in-law. The whole incident unfolds slowly through conversations where the trio (Joe and in-laws) go on with their lives. However, there is a secret between Joe and his dead fiance which he is afraid to tell in order to avoid hurting the in-laws.

The whole journey of dealing with grief, being empathetic, staying strong and showing courage in the tough times makes this movie therapeutic for the viewers. The pace of the story is slow, making it a bit boring in the beginning. However, the patience bore fruits, and I felt more connected to the emotions of Joe and grieving in-laws as the story developed. Despite the heaviness of the incident, the ending leaves the viewer with sweetness of love and life

This movie should be watched many times. I recommend it with 5 stars.

item.title: After The Quake
item.description:
A short collection of stories by Haruki Murakami written around a big earthquake that destroys Tokyo. In all the stories characters struggle through their regular life problems and emotional issues, where the tides turn when the earthquake hit the city. Despite the tragic situation, Murakami managed to keep characters positive with thoughtful endings.

There is also a story, the best one in my view, where a frog tries to convince a lonely hard-working man that his morals are important to save the world from earthquake, but ending is surprising. So to know the ending, I encourage you to read the book. It's a short one (less than 200 pages), and I finished it in around two hours by listening it on self-hosted Kokoro text to voice agent.

Despite the positives, the break in story made the book a bit boring, so I wont pick up again second time. I can only give it 3 stars.

item.title: One Hundred Years of Solitude
item.description:
Imagine a story where a young couple who are distant cousins wants to get married but the family warns them that if they do it, their offspring will be born with a pig's tail and die a horrible death. They both become worry but in the end, you can guess, they did not take the superstitious warning seriously and along with friends move to a distant place where they build a small village, Macondo. In following years, they (Buendia family) have three children and none of them is born with a pig's tail. They live happily, for first twenty years in which many people from far land including gypsies regularly visit Macondo. However, after those peaceful years, the remote Macondo start seeing a wave of globalization where government tries to control it. The political turmoil erupts and goes on for next eighty years during which seven generations pass and Macondo sees its first telegraph, train, industry and war. Although most of the story looks trivial, the regular visits of dead people, premonitions, invisibility and time running in a loop give it a touch for which this book is known. It is impossible to predict what will happen next, and the ending leaves reader in awe and fear. This might be the reason that the book won 1982 Nobel Prize in literature.

The book is moderate in size and quite addictive, at least for first half. There is a significant change in second half where many new characters emerge for a brief period. Reading them was quite boring. However, the overall story telling is neat, less cluttered with details, and has a poetic touch. This is the core strength of the book where author describes mundane things in such a beautiful manner that the lines stay with the reader. One example is:

One night he sang. Macondo woke up in a kind of angelic stupor that was caused by a zither that deserved more than this world and a voice that led one to believe that no other person on earth could feel such love. Pietro Crespi then saw the lights go on in every window in town except that of Amaranta.

Even though due to ADHD I usually struggle with fiction, this book was an easy read. It has a deeper impact on me, especially the tragedies revolving around the Buendia family. I highly recommend it. 5 stars

item.title: What I Talk About When I Talk About Running
item.description:
This is a memoir of Haruki Murakami, I mentioned about in the previous book post. Here the author describes his journey of becoming a novelist from a bar owner and how sport activities, especially running, helped him in doing so. He became a serious long distance runner in his early thirties while prior to that time he was rarely active. So reading his journey was inspiring. The author revealed many nuances for amateur runners that can be helpful in developing long-distance running habit—at least it was helpful for me. For instance:

The main thing was not the speed or distance so much as running every day, without taking a break.

It is a short book so one can finish it in a single read. However, I took it slow because I did not want this book to end. Reading it inspired me and gave me a new understanding of long-distance running. I highly recommend it with 4 stars.

item.title: Hear the Wind Sing
item.description:
This is the second book of Murakami I am reading, which I finished before finishing the first one. I was impressed by his writing style while reading his memoir where he mentioned about this book. So I decided to check his first creation as a writer.

It's a short book without any concrete story. The protagonist discusses mundane events of his daily life, such as meeting with friends and dating girls. So overall it is a bit boring. However, whats amazing is that it showed how Murakami build himself from this writing style to what he is known for. That's why I have read it.

So you can read it if you are free and looking for passing time. I recommend it with 3 stars.

item.title: The Green Mile
item.description:
This movie is impressive due to two reasons: first one is the storytelling in a nostalgic manner with a balanced approach to magic realism. The second one is a strong star cast, especially Tom Hanks. His acting is always fascinating due to his ability to deal with complex scenes, with hard emotions. I have seen a very few actors who can do that.

The story revolves around the protagonist, Paul Edgecomb, the head of a prison, who witnesses healing powers of a falsely acquitted African man. He learns from his first hand experiences that the African man is innocent but he can not do anything. It is a complicated situation where he is bound to do his duty while it is also wrong to swing the death sentence of an innocent man with divine powers. This dilemma leads to situations which has deep impact on you (the viewer), and for which you should watch the movie.

I loved every minute of the movie. Highly recommend it. 5 stars.
